sources.title: How to set up proactive engagement
Set up and manage planning groups
Create and schedule a shift plan
Workforce management security roles in the Workforce Engagement Management app (preview)
Best practices for configuring AI agents

notes.title: Build outbound engagement around identity and contact preferences
notes.body:
Start with provisioned channels and choose how customer records enter the engagement: file, API or an enabled Customer Insights journey. Configure the outbound workstream and engagement's queue, skills and identity key. A stable external contact identifier should map to the selected eligible Contact attribute so repeated imports update the same person. Review generated routing rather than maintaining unrelated parallel rules.

Before delivery, configure quiet hours, frequency and opt-outs. Customer-local evaluation needs the timezone supplied in the input; the system does not infer it from a phone number. Technical implicit opt-in is not evidence of legally required consent. Test suppressed contacts alongside ordinary deliveries, and use the channel-specific consent records when honoring a do-not-contact request.

notes.title: Choose dial behavior for the intended service experience
notes.body:
Preview, progressive, predictive and Copilot modes make different tradeoffs. Preview notifies a representative first and supports reviewing the customer before the call; manual or delayed start is specific to the documented Teams Phone extensibility setup. In the documented ACS preview path, the call starts after acceptance.

Progressive uses available representatives to pace calls; predictive adjusts dialing against capacity and performance; Copilot starts with an AI agent and escalates when needed. Treat these as operational choices, not blanket permission to automate any campaign. The dial-mode article restricts specified automated modes for commercial marketing/sales and flags telecommunications compliance concerns. Review purpose, consent and applicable requirements before use, then validate the representative and customer experience with a small service-outreach pilot.

notes.title: Enable outbound monitoring before interpreting campaign results
notes.body:
A configured engagement does not automatically establish dashboard access. Enable real-time analytics for proactive engagement and give the operator the documented Omnichannel Supervisor role. Open the Proactive Engagement dashboard and use its engagement, queue, timezone and business-unit filters to establish the scope of the view.

Read metrics by their definitions. Pending work has not yet been attempted; in-progress deliveries are active; throughput measures deliveries processed over the last hour. A completed delivery has reached a final intended outcome, which can include the end of attempts, so it is not interchangeable with a live-person connection. Use connect rate and live-person measures when the operational question is whether outreach actually reaches people.

notes.title: Establish workforce scope and access before planning
notes.body:
Install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package, then prepare the relevant users and planning scope. Copilot Service workspace continues to use its Omnichannel roles. The separate Workforce Engagement Management app is preview and introduces dedicated roles; a WFM Forecaster can manage forecasts without permission to publish schedules. Assign roles for the surface and duties actually used.

Define planning groups around queue/channel demand, timezone and service objectives. The group links forecast, capacity and shift plans so staffing assumptions stay aligned. A queue/channel combination belongs to only one planning group at a time, preventing duplicated demand. This staffing scope differs from a representative's per-conversation capacity profile: one plans required coverage, while the other constrains assignment workload.

notes.title: Turn historical demand into a reproducible staffing input
notes.body:
A forecast scenario defines entity, channels, queues, timezone and history, then predicts interaction volume and average handle time. A capacity plan uses forecast demand and service objectives to estimate staffing. When a planning group is selected, its timezone and demand fields populate the scenario and become read-only, keeping plans aligned.

For an external data source, upload history before scenario creation and plan a deliberate refresh process: automatic refresh is unavailable for that source. Saving a scenario does not prove a successful run. Check job history, inspect output, and use a new snapshot where supported to reflect updated history. Validate the input scope and run status before interpreting an unexpected staffing result; this is demand planning, not a decision about an individual employee.

notes.title: Publish schedules and synchronize external workforce data deliberately
notes.body:
Build a shift plan from the required skills, queues, calendar and activity itinerary, using a capacity plan when forecast-based coverage is required. Schedule representatives, inspect the resulting board, then publish the selected schedule. Editing a committed booking returns it to Unpublished, so republish the change rather than assuming the representative already sees the update.

If another workforce tool remains authoritative, use a defined Dataverse API integration for schedules and assignments, and provide operational data back to that tool where needed. Establish service-to-service authentication, data ownership, synchronization frequency and error handling. Schedule imports and real-time adherence have different freshness needs. Handle rate limits and transient failures with backoff; increasing request rate during throttling risks making the integration less reliable.

notes.title: Test AI delays and failures as part of the customer journey
notes.body:
Give the customer an initial greeting before beginning a potentially slow data lookup. Configure an appropriate latency message and examine connector or flow performance rather than leaving silence unexplained. Design retries, alternative paths and representative escalation for failed or incomplete tool responses.

For commitments or sensitive actions, prompts alone are insufficient enforcement. Use deterministic controls and the required human approval path. Test the full workflow under realistic telephony, background-noise, language and tool-failure conditions, then monitor latency, task completion and escalation after rollout. A successful demonstration of the happy path does not establish reliability across all callers or operating conditions.

cards.prompt: For repeated outbound uploads from an external CRM, what should the selected Contact unique identifier represent?
cards.answer: The external system’s stable identifier stored in an eligible Contact attribute.
cards.explanation: Matching the intended key allows update-or-insert behavior without creating a new contact for every delivery.

cards.prompt: Does proactive engagement infer the customer’s local timezone from the telephone number for quiet-hour evaluation?
cards.answer: No. Supply the supported timezone value in the uploaded data or API payload.
cards.explanation: If the local-timezone option is selected and the value is absent, the documented fallback is UTC.

cards.prompt: A new system receives a migrated voice outreach list that includes customers who previously opted out. Which setup preserves those existing preferences before delivery?
cards.answer: Import the existing do-not-call records into Voice consent for the corresponding contact points.
cards.explanation: Bulk upload the migrated do-not-call records into the correct voice consent scope. Text consent governs another consent channel; contact identity alone does not recreate opt-outs, and an opt-out for a different contact point does not suppress the intended number.

options.text: Import the opt-outs as Text consent records for the same telephone contact points.
Import the existing do-not-call records into Voice consent for the corresponding contact points.
Import the customers as contacts and rely on their identity mapping to recreate previous opt-outs.
Import the opt-outs as Voice consent for a different telephone contact point on each customer.

cards.prompt: Which dial mode starts the interaction with the workstream’s AI agent when the customer answers?
cards.answer: Copilot dial mode.
cards.explanation: The AI agent can escalate if necessary; this describes the technical flow rather than approval for every outreach purpose.

cards.prompt: Which documented telephony setup supports manual or delayed start for preview calls after representative acceptance?
cards.answer: Teams Phone extensibility.
cards.explanation: The documented ACS preview behavior starts automatically after acceptance; do not generalize the manual-start choice across both paths.

cards.prompt: A service team using Teams Phone extensibility requires a representative to inspect each customer’s case and decide when to place the call. Which configuration most directly fits?
cards.answer: Representative-led Preview with Manual start.
cards.explanation: Preview and manual start support deliberate review. Progressive/predictive automate pacing, while Copilot begins with AI.

options.text: Representative-led Predictive with automatic pacing.
AI-led Copilot mode.
Representative-led Progressive mode.
Representative-led Preview with Manual start.

cards.prompt: What role does the Proactive Engagement dashboard document for its operator?
cards.answer: Omnichannel Supervisor.
cards.explanation: Configured proactive engagement and enabled real-time analytics are also prerequisites.

cards.prompt: What time period does the proactive dashboard’s Throughput measure describe?
cards.answer: Deliveries processed over the last hour.
cards.explanation: Throughput measures processing pace, not the number of live people reached.

cards.prompt: A supervisor wants to assess whether outbound attempts successfully reach customers. Which dashboard measure best matches that question?
cards.answer: Connect rate.
cards.explanation: Connect rate compares connected deliveries with attempted deliveries. Pending and in-progress counts show workload, while throughput measures processing pace.

options.text: Connect rate.
Total unique engagements pending.
Throughput.
Deliveries in progress.

cards.prompt: Which package must an administrator install before using the documented workforce-management capabilities?
cards.answer: Workforce Management for Customer Service.
cards.explanation: Install it through Power Platform admin center; individual feature and user-access configuration still follows.

cards.prompt: Do the preview Workforce Engagement Management app’s dedicated WFM roles replace Omnichannel roles in Copilot Service workspace?
cards.answer: No. They apply within the separate preview app.
cards.explanation: Existing workspace role behavior continues; configure access according to the actual app surface.

cards.prompt: A team tries to add a queue/channel combination to a second planning group and receives a validation error. Which design change follows the documented planning boundary?
cards.answer: Keep that queue/channel combination in one planning group and associate its planning artifacts there.
cards.explanation: A queue/channel combination belongs to only one planning group at a time. Different timezones, separate capacity plans or additional forecast scenarios do not remove that demand-scope uniqueness rule.

options.text: Give the second planning group a different timezone while retaining the same queue/channel combination.
Associate a separate capacity plan with each overlapping planning group.
Keep that queue/channel combination in one planning group and associate its planning artifacts there.
Create separate forecast scenarios so each overlapping group counts the same queue/channel combination.

cards.prompt: What is the difference between a forecast scenario and a workforce capacity plan?
cards.answer: The forecast predicts demand; the capacity plan converts demand and service objectives into staffing requirements.
cards.explanation: Keep demand estimation separate from the settings that constrain an individual representative’s routing workload.

cards.prompt: Is forecast Auto refresh available when the scenario uses an external data source?
cards.answer: No. The documented external-source scenario does not offer Auto refresh.
cards.explanation: Prepare the uploaded history and manage subsequent refresh/output versions deliberately.

cards.prompt: A forecast scenario’s timezone, channels and queues are read-only after the planner selects a planning group. Where should the planner investigate the governing demand configuration?
cards.answer: The associated planning group.
cards.explanation: When a planning group is selected, timezone, channels and queues inherit its configuration and become read-only. Refresh timing, history source and forecast type govern other aspects of prediction rather than the inherited demand scope.

options.text: The forecast refresh schedule and its selected run-time slot.
The associated planning group.
The scenario's internal or external historical-data source selection.
The short-term or long-term forecast type selected at creation.

cards.prompt: What happens after a Committed workforce booking is edited?
cards.answer: It becomes Unpublished and must be republished for the update to be available.
cards.explanation: An edit is not automatically a new published schedule.

cards.prompt: Which API platform does the Learn integration unit describe for sharing workforce data with an external WFM system?
cards.answer: Dataverse API.
cards.explanation: It supports scenarios such as importing schedules and exporting interaction or adherence data; the integration still needs authentication and data mapping.

cards.prompt: A third-party workforce synchronization job encounters Dataverse throttling during peak load. Which response matches the documented integration guidance?
cards.answer: Retry transient failures using exponential backoff.
cards.explanation: The integration guidance explicitly recommends retries with exponential backoff for rate limits and transient failures. Immediate retries or synchronized short-delay retries continue pressure; handling authentication errors alone omits the throttling recovery path.

options.text: Retry each throttled request immediately until one attempt succeeds.
Retry all affected workers together after the same fixed short delay.
Retry authentication failures only and leave throttled requests for the next full synchronization.
Retry transient failures using exponential backoff.

cards.prompt: What should a voice agent do before starting a potentially slow customer-data lookup?
cards.answer: Play an initial greeting and use appropriate latency messaging.
cards.explanation: Acknowledge the caller while lookup work proceeds instead of creating unexplained silence.

cards.prompt: Are system prompts alone sufficient to enforce sensitive financial commitments by a real-time agent?
cards.answer: No. Use deterministic controls and appropriate human review or approval.
cards.explanation: The transparency note describes confident incorrect commitments and limitations of prompt-only constraints.

cards.prompt: A voice agent works in normal tests but stalls when a lookup tool times out. Which change addresses the documented reliability concern?
cards.answer: Add and test a recovery path that can retry, offer alternatives or escalate to a representative.
cards.explanation: Tool failures are expected design cases. Removing delays from testing or assuming successful responses leaves the failure path unhandled.

options.text: Add and test a recovery path that can retry, offer alternatives or escalate to a representative.
Test only the successful lookup path to keep evaluation consistent.
Increase confidence in the system prompt without changing recovery logic.
Remove representative escalation so the agent must complete every lookup.
